purpose: How a working gold-plating bench keeps each commercial gold and support bath inside its supplier-TDS operating window: reasoning from what gold content, pH, temperature, agitation and additive balance each do to the deposit, reading drift signatures early, choosing the right analysis method class (titration, Hull cell, coupon + XRF, supplier lab), replenishing little-and-often instead of crash-correcting, and running the bath log as the evidence base that decides watch, correct, or escalate.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
every bath is a purchased commercial plating product operated per its supplier technical data sheet; the TDS of the specific product and lot governs every setpoint
operating parameters are taught as mechanisms and qualitative bands; a published handbook-class range is referenced only as a handbook-class range, never as a universal setpoint
cyanide-bearing chemistry is maintained only by formally trained persons under the jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules; safety appears as obligation classes, never improvised procedure
the shop plates intermittently at jeweler bench scale, so idle-bath drift, small-batch analysis economics and supplier-lab turnaround are first-class concerns
exclusions: choosing which gold system to run per job — bath families (alkaline cyanide, neutral and acid hard gold, sulfite/non-cyanide, electroless/immersion), color/karat alloying as a selection lever, strike vs color vs build roles, support-bath classes and substrate matching belong to the sibling bath-selection KB

contamination diagnosis and cure — drag-in/drag-out control, metallic and organic contamination signatures, filtration and carbon treatment execution, carbonate freeze-out, bath aging disposition, regenerate-vs-replace economics and gold recovery belong to the sibling contamination-and-lifecycle KB
DIY bath formulation from raw chemicals — this KB assumes purchased commercial plating products only; compounding a bath from cyanide or gold salts is out of scope everywhere

asserting universal numeric setpoints for temperature, pH, gold concentration, current density or additive dosage — setpoints come from the specific product's TDS, and analysis results are method-class readings checked against that window, never asserted numeric truths

improvised safety or waste procedure — cyanide and acid handling, storage, segregation, ventilation and disposal are obligation classes routed to formal training and the jurisdiction's rules; spent-bath and rinse disposal is the lifecycle KB's regulated-waste territory
rectifier setup, fixturing, current-distribution and thickness delivery on parts — the process-execution specialist's territory; this KB verifies the bath, not the run
surface preparation, cleaning lines and rinse-cascade design — the surface-prep specialist's territory, consulted only when a deposit fault must be routed away from chemistry
personalized legal, medical or financial advice — exposure and allergy topics route to regulation classes and professional care

competency_questions.question: What does the supplier TDS govern for my specific gold bath, and how do I turn it into a bench control card I can actually work from?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TDS_WINDOW_BASELINE names the parameters the TDS windows (temperature, pH, metal content, current density, agitation, additives, trim and replenisher chemicals) and describes extracting them into a per-bath control card that governs every later control action

competency_questions.question: What does each bath parameter — gold content, pH, temperature, agitation, additive balance — actually do to the deposit, and what happens as each one drifts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PARAMETER_EFFECT_MAP states each parameter's deposit effect as a mechanism (e.g. metal content sets the burning threshold, agitation feeds the cathode film) with the drift symptom each produces, and TEMP_AGITATION_CONTROL covers the thermal and mass-transfer levers without invented setpoints

competency_questions.question: How do I know how much gold my runs have consumed, and when and how much to replenish?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOLD_CONTENT_CONTROL explains ampere-minute bookkeeping as a Faraday-based estimate verified by analysis and coupon, and REPLENISH_LITTLE_OFTEN sizes additions per the TDS replenisher scheme against that bookkeeping

competency_questions.question: How is pH watched and corrected safely on cyanide and acid gold baths, and what is the non-negotiable safety line?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PH_CONTROL_DISCIPLINE gives the drift directions and TDS-sanctioned trim chemicals, and CYANIDE_SAFETY_ENVELOPE states the hard line: cyanide and acids never mix, never share storage or a drain, and alkalinity/pH floors are published-chemistry stop conditions, with formal-training and jurisdiction pointers

competency_questions.question: Which deposit changes are early warnings that the bath is drifting, and how do I tell chemistry drift from a prep or process fault before I touch the bath?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DRIFT_SIGNATURE_READING maps signatures (color shift, haze onset, burning threshold creeping down, rising cell voltage, slowing rate) to the parameter class that moves them and gives the routing test that keeps prep/process faults from being treated as chemistry

competency_questions.question: Which analysis method class answers which question about the bath, and what are each method's limits?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TITRATION_ANALYSIS, HULL_CELL_PANEL, COUPON_XRF_CHECK and SUPPLIER_LAB_SERVICE each state what the method measures, what it cannot tell you, and that results are readings checked against the TDS window rather than asserted truths

competency_questions.question: How often should each bath check run for my throughput, and which events force an out-of-schedule check?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ANALYSIS_CADENCE_PLAN assigns each method class a cadence tied to throughput and names the upset triggers (defect appears, correction made, idle period ends) that pull a check forward

competency_questions.question: Why is little-and-often replenishment the discipline, and how is each addition sized, made and recorded?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REPLENISH_LITTLE_OFTEN argues the mechanism (small in-window doses avoid the overshoot/counter-dose oscillation), sizes doses from bookkeeping plus analysis per the TDS scheme, and requires each addition logged at the tank when made

competency_questions.question: The bath has drifted badly — how is a large correction staged, and what must be true before customer work resumes?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CRASH_CORRECTION_PROTOCOL stages the correction in TDS-sized increments with analysis between and one variable at a time, and OUT_OF_WINDOW_RESPONSE holds customer work until in-window analysis plus a clean test piece prove recovery

competency_questions.question: What belongs in the bath log, and how does it become the evidence base that catches drift no single run shows?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BATH_LOG_EVIDENCE lists the mandatory per-run fields (ampere-minutes, temperature, pH, additions, analyses, deposit observation) and TREND_REVIEW_DECISION shows how periodic reading of the log separates slow drift from special-cause upsets and decides watch, correct, or escalate

competency_questions.question: How do additive and hardener balance control hardness, brightness and hue, and why are they dosed only per TDS and analysis?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ADDITIVE_HARDENER_BALANCE explains hardener metal co-deposition as the hardness-and-hue mechanism in hard golds, proprietary brighteners as TDS-governed unknowns, and the rule that no additive is dosed on a hunch

competency_questions.question: How do evaporation, byproduct build-up and plain idleness change a bath that is not even plating, and what is verified before the first customer run afterward?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EVAPORATION_VOLUME_CONTROL covers concentration-by-evaporation and make-up water discipline, CARBONATE_BYPRODUCT_WATCH covers byproduct accumulation as a monitored mechanism, and IDLE_BATH_RESTART requires level, pH, analysis and a test coupon before customer work after an idle period

competency_questions.question: Which questions does this KB deliberately refuse to answer, and where does each route?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MAINTENANCE_SCOPE_BOUNDARY routes bath-family and selection questions to the selection KB, contamination diagnosis and lifecycle economics to the lifecycle KB, forbids DIY formulation outright, and keeps analysis results as method-class readings against the TDS window

glossary.definition: The supplier's document for a specific commercial bath product: its operating windows, replenisher and trim chemicals, analysis scheme and troubleshooting notes. In this KB the TDS is the setpoint authority — the shop refines within it, never against it.

The TDS-defined band for each controlled parameter (temperature, pH, metal content, current density, agitation, additive level) inside which the deposit meets spec; a bath outside any window is not used for customer work until brought back and verified.

Faraday-based accounting of the charge passed through the bath, used to estimate gold consumed and to size replenishment between analyses; an estimate that must be reconciled against analysis and witness coupons because cathode efficiency drifts with bath age.

The current density above which metal ions cannot reach the cathode film fast enough and the deposit burns (dark, rough, matte at edges); it falls as metal content falls and rises with temperature and agitation, which is why burning at yesterday's settings signals bath drift.

A small trapezoidal bench cell that plates one panel across a sweep of current densities, showing the bath's bright range, haze and burning onset on a single coupon; a fast qualitative diagnostic, not a concentration measurement.
A sacrificial test piece plated under production conditions and measured (typically by XRF) to prove the bath's real deposition rate and deposit quality before customer pieces are risked.

The recognizable deposit or cell change — hue shift, haze onset, burning threshold creeping down, rising voltage at fixed current, slowing rate — that betrays which parameter class is moving before any titration is run.
The discipline of making small, TDS-sized additions on a bookkeeping-and-analysis cadence so the bath never leaves its window, instead of letting it drift and then dosing heavily.

The staged, analysis-gated restoration of a badly drifted bath — small increments, one variable at a time, test panel between steps; the expensive failure mode that little-and-often replenishment exists to prevent.

Uncomplexed cyanide in alkaline gold baths that keeps the gold complex stable and suppresses non-adherent immersion deposits; a titrated control parameter that is simultaneously a safety-class material — its bath must stay strongly alkaline because published chemistry converts free cyanide toward lethal HCN gas as pH falls.

nodes.definition: Establish the supplier's technical data sheet as the governing document for each bath on the line and extract it into a bench control card the operator can work from at the tank: the windowed parameters (temperature, pH, metal content, current density, agitation), the named replenisher and trim chemicals, the supplier's analysis scheme and its stated frequencies, and the product and lot identity the card belongs to. The card is what makes 'in window' a checkable statement rather than folklore; every later control action in this KB compares a reading to this card, and the card is rebuilt whenever the supplier revises the TDS or the shop changes product or lot. No parameter value on the card is invented — each one traces to a TDS line.

excluded: choosing which bath product to buy (selection KB)
inventing setpoints the TDS does not state

pros.claim: A control card at the tank turns every drift argument into a comparison against the supplier's own window
pros.example: when an operator insists the acid gold 'runs better warmer', the card shows the TDS temperature band and the discussion becomes whether the reading is inside it

cons.claim: A card copied once and never rebuilt silently governs with a stale window after a product or TDS change
cons.example: the shop switches to a new hard-gold product whose hardener window differs, but the old card stays taped to the tank and additions follow it

failure_modes: running the bath from memory or a forum post instead of the specific product's TDS
one generic card serving two different products because both are 'acid gold'
card values edited by hand to match shop habit rather than the TDS
acceptance_tests: every controlled parameter on the card carries a TDS-sourced window and the TDS names the trim/replenisher chemical for it; the card states product name, lot and TDS revision date
revisit_triggers: the supplier issues a revised TDS or replenisher scheme
the shop changes bath product, supplier or lot
logged shop runs repeatedly sit at one edge of a TDS window

base.update_signal: a TDS revision, product change or supplier scheme change lands on the bench

nodes.definition: Bound every analysis, correction and addition inside the safety envelope that bath maintenance work inherits: cyanide-bearing baths, their rinses and their drains are physically and procedurally segregated from every acid — never mixed, never stored together, never sharing a drain — because published chemistry converts cyanide toward lethal HCN gas on acid contact, and the alkalinity floor of a cyanide bath is therefore a stop condition, not a tuning suggestion. Acid gold baths carry their own published-chemistry pH floor below which HCN liberates. PPE, ventilation, labeling, locked storage and emergency readiness are obligation classes; anyone titrating or dosing these baths holds formal training, and the jurisdiction's workplace and hazmat rules are verified rather than assumed. This node is content, not an aside: it constrains which corrections are even considerable.

included: cyanide/acid segregation as an absolute line for maintenance work
pH and alkalinity floors as published-chemistry stop conditions
PPE, ventilation, storage, labeling and training as obligation classes
excluded: improvised or step-by-step emergency procedure (formal training territory)
waste characterization and disposal execution (lifecycle KB and safety specialist)

pros.claim: Treating the safety envelope as a constraint on corrections removes whole classes of fatal shortcuts before they are proposed
pros.example: a fast 'fix' for high pH in an alkaline gold bath by adding acid is not weighed against schedule pressure — it is not on the menu at all

cons.claim: Obligation-class guidance cannot substitute for local rules and training, so it must keep pointing outward instead of answering
cons.example: the KB can say cyanide storage is a locked, segregated, jurisdiction-governed class but cannot tell a Berlin shop its exact licensing regime

failure_modes: pH trim of a cyanide bath attempted with an acid because it was within reach
cyanide bath rinse water routed to the same drain as pickle rinses
an untrained helper left to run the weekly free-cyanide titration
acceptance_tests: no maintenance instruction in the shop's SOPs brings an acid near a cyanide bath, its rinses or its drain; alkalinity/pH floors appear as stop conditions; every person doing bath analysis or dosing holds documented formal training and the jurisdiction check is recorded
revisit_triggers: a new chemical, tank, drain or layout change enters the bath area
staffing changes put a new person on analysis or dosing duty
the jurisdiction's workplace or hazmat rules change

base.update_signal: any change to chemicals, layout, staffing or jurisdiction rules touching the bath area

nodes.definition: Hold the mechanism map that makes bath readings meaningful: gold content sets the limiting current density, so a depleting bath burns at settings that worked last week and plates slower; pH governs complex stability, cathode efficiency and deposit character, and in acid golds it also steers hue while carrying a published-chemistry safety floor; temperature moves efficiency, brightness, hardness and color together, which is why 'a bit warmer' is never a free improvement; agitation feeds metal to the cathode film and is the lever that raises usable current density in diffusion-limited acid golds; additive and hardener balance sets grain, brightness, hardness and hue. The map is mechanism knowledge — what moves what, in which direction, with which deposit symptom — and deliberately contains no setpoints, because those live on the TDS control card.

included: direction-of-effect mechanisms for gold content, pH, temperature, agitation, additives
the deposit symptom each drifting parameter produces
interaction awareness (several parameters move color together)
excluded: numeric setpoints (TDS card)
which bath family exhibits which chemistry (selection KB)

pros.claim: Mechanism knowledge lets one bench read generalize across every commercial product without inventing numbers
pros.example: knowing low metal content lowers the burning threshold explains scorched edges on both an alkaline soft gold and an acid hard gold, whatever their TDS values

cons.claim: Because several parameters move the same symptom, the map alone cannot pick the culprit without analysis
cons.example: a dull deposit could be byproduct accumulation, organic load or a temperature excursion — the map narrows, the titration or lab decides

failure_modes: memorizing one bath's numbers as if they were the mechanism
single-cause thinking when two parameters drifted together
treating hue as a cosmetic issue instead of the coupled output of hardener, pH, temperature and current density
acceptance_tests: for each controlled parameter the operator can state its direction of effect on the deposit and the symptom of drift in each direction, without citing a single invented number
revisit_triggers: the shop's logged runs contradict a taught direction of effect
a new bath chemistry class enters the line with different parameter behavior
supplier technical guidance refines a mechanism

base.update_signal: shop log evidence or supplier guidance contradicting a taught parameter effect

nodes.definition: Police the edges of the maintenance role so its answers stay honest: questions about which gold system, strike or support bath to run, or how to move color by alloying, route to bath-selection expertise; a fault that persists while every parameter reads in-window, or any question about drag-out control, filtration, carbon treatment, bath aging, regenerate-vs-replace or gold recovery, routes to contamination-and-lifecycle expertise with the bath log attached; no request, however urgent, is answered with DIY formulation from raw chemicals — the menu is commercial products per their TDS; and every analysis output is reported as a method-class reading checked against the TDS window, never as an asserted numeric truth about gold baths in general. Routing with the evidence attached is itself expert work: the log is what makes the receiving specialist effective.

included: routing rules to selection and lifecycle scopes
handing off with the log attached
excluded: performing the routed work (selection, contamination cure, recovery)
waste disposal decisions

pros.claim: Clean routing stops the maintenance reflex — another dose — from being applied to problems replenishment cannot fix
pros.example: a gray, dull deposit with all parameters in window is handed to contamination diagnosis instead of receiving a third brightener addition

cons.claim: Boundary discipline adds a handoff step that can feel slow on a one-person bench where the same jeweler wears every hat
cons.example: the solo plater must consciously switch from 'dose it' to 'diagnose it as contamination' even though no second person exists to hand to

failure_modes: replenishing an aging bath ever harder instead of raising the lifecycle question
improvising chemistry from raw salts under deadline pressure
quoting a bench titration number as a universal fact about gold baths
acceptance_tests: each out-of-scope question class has a named destination (selection, lifecycle, safety, process execution) and handoffs carry the relevant log extract
revisit_triggers: repeated boundary disputes over the same question class
a sibling KB's scope changes

base.update_signal: a boundary dispute recurs or a sibling scope is redefined

nodes.definition: Track the bath's gold inventory as it is spent: every ampere-minute of plating removes gold from solution, so charge bookkeeping gives a running Faraday-based estimate of metal consumed since the last addition — an estimate, because cathode efficiency differs by chemistry class and falls with bath age, which is why the bookkeeping is periodically reconciled against a gold analysis and a measured witness coupon. Depletion has a face the bench must recognize before any analysis: the burning threshold creeps down so edges scorch at settings that plated clean last week, and rate falls so pieces come out thin for their time. Keeping gold inside the TDS band by scheduled small additions is both quality control and money control — the metal in solution is the shop's most valuable consumable.

included: ampere-minute bookkeeping as a Faraday-based estimate
excluded: drag-out reduction techniques and gold recovery (lifecycle KB)
thickness delivery on parts (process execution)

pros.claim: Bookkeeping catches depletion between analyses, when the bath still looks fine
pros.example: after a week of heavy bracelet work the log shows enough ampere-minutes to warrant a scheduled dose before the Friday customer batch, though no defect has appeared yet

cons.claim: Uncorrected bookkeeping quietly diverges from reality as efficiency drifts with bath age
cons.example: an aging acid hard gold consumes charge at falling efficiency, so the estimate overstates gold used and additions slowly overshoot until a coupon exposes the gap

failure_modes: no charge record kept, so gold status is guessed from deposit color alone
bookkeeping trusted for months without a reconciling analysis or coupon
additions sized by round numbers instead of the TDS replenisher scheme
acceptance_tests: a running ampere-minute tally exists per bath, each reconciliation against analysis or coupon is dated, and the current divergence between estimate and measurement is known
revisit_triggers: a coupon or analysis contradicts the bookkeeping estimate
throughput or typical piece mix changes materially

base.update_signal: a reconciliation reveals estimate-vs-measurement divergence beyond the shop's tolerance

nodes.definition: Run pH as a disciplined loop: a calibrated meter (buffer-calibrated on a schedule, calibration logged), knowledge of each bath's natural drift direction, and correction only with the trim chemical the TDS names. Acid hard golds drift downward in service — the insoluble anode's oxygen evolution generates acid — so the watch is against the TDS floor, which sits above the published-chemistry line where HCN liberates; alkaline cyanide baths must stay strongly alkaline at all times, with the published alkalinity floor treated as a stop condition and trim only ever upward with the TDS-named alkali. pH moves efficiency, deposit character and, in hard golds, hue, so an uncalibrated meter does not merely mislead — it launches corrections against phantom drift. Any reading at or beyond a floor stops plating immediately; that is a safety response, not a quality preference.

excluded: any acid use near cyanide chemistry (forbidden by the safety envelope)
choosing the bath's pH class (selection KB)

pros.claim: Knowing the natural drift direction turns a routine reading into an early warning with a known cause
pros.example: the acid gold reading near the low edge of its TDS band after a heavy week is expected anode-driven drift — trimmed per TDS before it approaches the floor

cons.claim: pH is a single scalar that hides which of several upstream causes moved it
cons.example: a fast downward step (rather than slow creep) suggests drag-in or an upset, not normal operation — the same reading demands a different response

failure_modes: trusting an uncalibrated meter and correcting phantom drift
trimming with a convenient chemical the TDS never sanctioned
plating through a floor reading to finish a job
acceptance_tests: meter calibration is on a logged schedule; each bath's card names its trim chemical and drift direction; the SOP states that a floor reading stops plating and what verification precedes restart
revisit_triggers: pH drifts opposite to the expected direction
trim consumption rises without a throughput rise

base.update_signal: a floor excursion, a reversed drift direction, or a calibration found stale

nodes.definition: Hold temperature and agitation as controlled variables rather than ambient conditions: the thermostat is verified against an independent thermometer because a failed or mis-set heater shifts efficiency, brightness, hardness and color together and can masquerade as chemistry drift; agitation is chosen and kept constant because it feeds metal to the cathode film and thereby sets the usable current density — especially in diffusion-limited acid hard golds, where stronger solution movement is the legitimate lever for faster work. The safety envelope constrains the method: air sparging into a cyanide bath is excluded because aerosolized mist is an exposure route and air absorption accelerates carbonate formation; stirrer, cathode-rod or work movement carry the duty instead. Changing either variable is a logged event, because both move the deposit and both silently reframe every other reading.

included: thermostat verification against an independent thermometer
agitation constancy and its mass-transfer role
logging any change to either variable
excluded: numeric temperature setpoints (TDS card)
rectifier and current-distribution work (process execution)

pros.claim: Verifying the thermostat removes the cheapest and most common impostor of chemistry drift
pros.example: a batch of dull pieces traces to a heater that stuck low overnight — found in one minute with the reference thermometer, no chemical touched

cons.claim: Constancy discipline makes tempting one-off tweaks (a quick warm-up to speed a late job) look harmless when they are not
cons.example: nudging the hard gold warmer to hurry a rush order also shifts hue and hardness, and the odd-colored batch costs more than the minutes saved

failure_modes: trusting the dial instead of a measured bath temperature
changing agitation between runs without recording it, corrupting every comparison
air-sparging a cyanide bath for convenience
acceptance_tests: bath temperature is verified against an independent thermometer on a logged cadence and every deliberate temperature or agitation change appears in the log with its reason
revisit_triggers: measured temperature disagrees with the controller
a fixturing or throughput change alters solution movement around the work

base.update_signal: a thermostat discrepancy or an agitation change enters the log

nodes.definition: Manage the smallest concentrations with the largest cosmetic authority: in hard golds the hardener metal (cobalt or nickel class) co-deposits at fractions of a percent and sets hardness and hue together — too little and the deposit goes soft and off-tone, too much and it turns brownish and brittle — so the hardener window on the TDS is narrow and additions are sized only from analysis; proprietary brighteners and grain refiners are unknowns by design, dosed strictly per the TDS scheme because their composition is not disclosed and their overdose signatures (haze, stress, dullness) mimic contamination; in alloyed color baths the alloy-metal balance drifts with use, so hue is checked against a retained color standard and trimmed per the supplier's recipe, never freestyled. The governing rule: no additive enters the bath without an analysis-backed or TDS-scheduled reason, because every unlogged 'shot' of brightener destroys the interpretability of the next drift signature.

included: hardener-metal window discipline in hard golds
alloy-balance hue checks against a retained standard
excluded: selecting color systems or karat targets (selection KB)
organic-contamination cure such as carbon treatment (lifecycle KB)

pros.claim: Analysis-gated dosing keeps the narrow hardener window from being wandered out of in either direction
pros.example: a slightly pale hard-gold deposit prompts a hardener analysis first — which shows the metal in window and points at pH instead, sparing the bath a harmful cobalt-class overdose

cons.claim: Dependence on supplier analysis schemes for proprietary additives leaves the bench partially blind between checks
cons.example: a brightener depleting faster than the TDS schedule assumes shows up first as creeping haze, not on any bench titration the shop can run

failure_modes: brightener dosed on appearance alone, masking the real cause
hardener trimmed toward a color preference until the deposit embrittles
two additive changes made together so neither effect is attributable
acceptance_tests: every additive addition in the log cites its analysis result or TDS schedule line; hue checks against the retained standard are dated; no two additive variables were changed in one step
revisit_triggers: hue drifts while hardener analysis reads in window
additive consumption departs from the TDS-projected rate
the supplier reformulates an additive

base.update_signal: an additive analysis contradicting appearance, or a supplier reformulation notice

nodes.definition: Watch the byproducts a bath makes by existing: alkaline cyanide golds grow carbonate continuously — the solution absorbs carbon dioxide from the air and oxidizes some of its own cyanide — and accumulated carbonate first dulls the deposit and drags efficiency before anything else reads out of window; acid golds accumulate breakdown products of their organic additives with a similar dulling, hazing endgame. The maintenance job is measurement and trend: carbonate or byproduct level is checked on the analysis cadence, its growth rate is logged so the shop can see treatment coming weeks ahead, and a dulling deposit is compared against the byproduct trend before any additive is dosed. Executing treatment — carbonate freeze-out, carbon treatment, partial remake — is deliberately excluded: those are lifecycle interventions, and this node's output is the evidenced trigger that sends the bath there at the right time rather than after quality has already collapsed.

included: carbonate growth as a mechanism in alkaline baths
organic-byproduct accumulation awareness in acid golds
trend logging and the treatment trigger
excluded: freeze-out, carbon treatment and remake execution (lifecycle KB)
contamination from external sources (lifecycle KB)

pros.claim: A byproduct trend converts a slow inevitable death into a scheduled, budgeted event
pros.example: the log's carbonate line rising month over month lets the shop plan the alkaline bath's treatment for a quiet week instead of discovering dull deposits mid-order

cons.claim: Byproduct dullness is easily confused with organic contamination, inviting the wrong routing
cons.example: a hazy deposit gets blamed on drag-in oils when the carbonate trend, unread, already explained it

failure_modes: no byproduct measurement until deposits already dull
dosing brightener against a byproduct problem it cannot fix
treating the byproduct trigger as optional because the bath 'still works'
acceptance_tests: the log carries a dated byproduct/carbonate trend for each susceptible bath and the treatment trigger level from the TDS or supplier guidance is written on the control card
revisit_triggers: byproduct growth rate changes without a throughput change
dullness appears while the byproduct trend still reads low

base.update_signal: a byproduct measurement crossing the supplier's treatment guidance level

nodes.definition: Control the denominator every concentration lives over: a heated bath loses water continuously, so everything dissolved in it concentrates between checks, and a low, concentrated bath can read rich in gold while actually holding the same metal in less water. The discipline is a marked working level on every tank, make-up to that level with the water quality the TDS specifies (deionized water as the default class, because tap minerals accumulate and never leave), level restored before any sample is drawn so analyses compare like with like, and make-up events logged. In cyanide practice the first still drag-out rinse is conventionally returned as part of evaporation make-up — that return belongs to this node's level arithmetic, while the design of drag-out capture itself stays with the lifecycle KB. Level is checked before interpretation: a surprising analysis on an unrestored bath is a measurement artifact until proven otherwise.

included: make-up water quality as a TDS class
excluded: drag-out capture design and gold recovery from rinses (lifecycle KB)
rinse-cascade engineering (surface-prep territory)

pros.claim: Restoring level before sampling removes the commonest source of self-inflicted analysis noise
pros.example: a hot week's evaporation made gold read high; topped to the mark first, the same titration shows the bath actually in window, and no false 'dilution correction' happens

cons.claim: Level discipline says nothing about what evaporation concentrated disproportionately
cons.example: restored volume brings gold back to its window while accumulated conducting salts remain elevated — only a fuller analysis exposes that

failure_modes: sampling a low bath and correcting the resulting artifact
topping up with tap water and accumulating minerals
no marked level, so 'full' depends on who looks
acceptance_tests: every heated tank carries a marked working level, make-up water class matches the TDS, and each analysis entry notes that level was restored before sampling
revisit_triggers: make-up volume trends upward (heater, ventilation or cover change)
an analysis was taken below the mark

base.update_signal: a sampling-below-level incident or a shift in evaporation rate

nodes.definition: Use the deposit and the cell as the first instruments: hue shifting warm or pale is the earliest visible flag of hardener, pH or alloy-balance movement; haze or dullness creeping in points at byproduct accumulation, organic load or a temperature excursion; the burning threshold walking down — scorched edges at settings that plated clean before — is the classic face of falling metal content or weakened agitation; rising cell voltage at fixed current and a slowing rate betray conductivity and efficiency drift. Each signature narrows the suspect list to a parameter class and dispatches the matching analysis before anything is added to the tank. The second half of the skill is routing: a fault localized to one rack position, one geometry or one entry event is process or prep, not chemistry — the drift reader's discipline is to prove the bath is the variable before the bath is touched, because dosing a healthy bath is how good chemistry gets ruined.

included: per-run deposit observation as standing practice
excluded: contamination signature diagnosis (lifecycle KB)
defect cause-tree adjudication on finished goods (quality specialist)

pros.claim: Signature reading buys days of warning at zero marginal cost — the pieces are being looked at anyway
pros.example: the operator notices this week's yellows run slightly warm against the retained color standard and schedules a hardener analysis before a single piece is rejectable

cons.claim: Signatures overlap, and eye-based reading varies with light and observer
cons.example: dull-and-slightly-dark can be byproduct load, organics or a cold bath — the signature alone cannot convict, and under warm shop lighting two operators disagree on 'slightly warm'

failure_modes: plating on for weeks without looking at the deposit critically
treating a one-rack-position defect as bath chemistry
acting on a signature directly with an addition instead of an analysis
acceptance_tests: each run's log entry carries a deposit observation against the retained standard, and any drift note names the suspected parameter class plus the analysis dispatched
revisit_triggers: a signature is diagnosed to the wrong parameter class twice
lighting or the retained color standard changes
a new chemistry class with unfamiliar signatures enters the line

base.update_signal: a misdiagnosed signature, or analysis repeatedly contradicting the bench read

nodes.definition: Run the wet-chemical bench methods as a class: titration answers 'how much of a titratable species is in solution' — free cyanide in alkaline golds by the silver-nitrate method, and the supplier test-kit determinations of gold or trim species the TDS scheme prescribes for the product. Its readings are method-class results checked against the TDS window: a titration is only as good as its endpoint recognition, reagent freshness and sampling, so a single surprising value triggers a repeat before it triggers a correction. Titrating a cyanide bath is itself cyanide handling — same training, PPE, segregation and bench discipline as the tank, with reagents that must never meet the cyanide sample stream's drain. What titration cannot see: trace metallic contaminants, additive breakdown products, or anything proprietary — those needs route to the supplier lab. The method earns its keep as the cheap, fast, in-house backbone of the cadence.

included: free-cyanide and supplier-kit determinations as method classes
excluded: trace-metal and proprietary-additive analysis (supplier lab)
asserting titration values as universal bath truths

pros.claim: In-house titration gives same-day answers that keep the little-and-often loop closed without waiting on a lab
pros.example: the weekly free-cyanide check comes back low against the TDS window and the trim dose goes in that afternoon, logged, instead of after a two-week lab round trip

cons.claim: Endpoint and sampling errors produce confident wrong numbers that then drive wrong doses
cons.example: a stale indicator shifts the apparent endpoint, the free-cyanide reading comes out high, and an unneeded 'correction' is nearly made before the repeat titration disagrees

failure_modes: correcting on a single unrepeated surprising titration
untrained hands running a cyanide determination
reagents stored or disposed of across the cyanide/acid segregation line
acceptance_tests: each titration entry records method, reagent lot and result against the TDS window; surprising values show a logged repeat; only trained, named persons run cyanide determinations
revisit_triggers: bench titrations diverge from supplier lab results
a reagent or method change in the supplier's scheme

base.update_signal: a bench-vs-lab divergence or a supplier method revision

nodes.definition: Use the Hull cell as the bath's one-glance portrait: a small trapezoidal cell plates a single panel across a continuous sweep of current densities, so one coupon shows where the bright range sits, where burning begins, and whether haze, streaking or dullness lives at the low or high end — a pattern the trained eye maps straight onto parameter classes. Its power at the jeweler bench is before/after proof: a panel run ahead of a correction and another after it show whether the correction did what the analysis predicted, without risking a customer piece. Its limits are equally definite: the panel is qualitative, drawn from a small sample that may not represent a poorly mixed tank, and its conditions must mimic production (same temperature, comparable agitation) or its story is about the cell, not the bath. A clean panel with dull production work is itself diagnostic — it points the fault away from chemistry toward prep or process.

excluded: quantitative concentration determination (titration or lab)
thickness certification (coupon + XRF)

pros.claim: One panel visualizes the whole current-density behavior of the bath at once, which no single plated piece can
pros.example: a panel whose bright band has narrowed from both ends confirms the suspicion that the bath, not the racking of one awkward pendant, is drifting

cons.claim: Panel reading is interpretive craft that novices over-read
cons.example: faint low-end haze on an otherwise healthy panel triggers a needless additive dose by an operator who has not seen enough normal panels

failure_modes: running the cell cold and diagnosing a phantom fault
skipping the after-correction panel so the correction's effect is never proven
treating one panel as a quantitative analysis
acceptance_tests: panels are run at production-representative temperature and noted agitation, filed with date and bath state, and every crash correction shows a before and after panel in the log
revisit_triggers: panel results repeatedly disagree with production outcomes
a new operator takes over panel reading

base.update_signal: panel-vs-production disagreement or an operator change on panel duty

nodes.definition: Prove the bath's real output with a witness coupon: a sacrificial piece plated under production conditions, measured by XRF for thickness, and inspected for color and quality, converts 'the bath should be plating at roughly its usual rate' into a measured fact. This is the reconciliation instrument for ampere-minute bookkeeping — efficiency drifts with bath age, and acid hard golds in particular run at markedly lower and more variable cathode efficiency than alkaline soft golds (a handbook-class behavior), so the time-per-thickness assumption must be re-anchored by measurement on a cadence and always after a correction or idle restart. XRF's own limits are part of the method class: it reads a small spot, geometry and curvature bias it, and thin multi-layer stacks need the instrument set up for them; a jeweler without in-house XRF runs the same discipline through a service lab or a supplier's measurement. The coupon is retained and filed — it is physical evidence attached to the log.

included: XRF thickness verification and its limits
rate re-anchoring after corrections and idle restarts
excluded: thickness specification per wear class and claim compliance (quality specialist)
in-solution concentration analysis (titration and lab)

pros.claim: The coupon catches efficiency drift that solution analysis alone cannot see
pros.example: gold titrates in window, yet the coupon shows the aging acid bath now delivers noticeably less thickness for the same ampere-minutes — the time tables get corrected before a customer bracelet ships thin

cons.claim: Coupons cost gold, time and access to measurement, so small shops under-run them
cons.example: a bench without its own XRF batches coupons to a monthly lab drop and flies blind on rate between drops

failure_modes: coupon plated at convenient rather than production conditions, proving nothing
no coupon after a crash correction before customer work resumes
XRF spot placed on unrepresentative geometry
acceptance_tests: each coupon entry records plating conditions, XRF result and the bookkeeping assumption it confirms or corrects; a coupon exists after every correction and idle restart before customer work
revisit_triggers: coupon rate diverges from the bookkeeping assumption
measurement access changes (instrument acquired, lab changed)

base.update_signal: a coupon-vs-bookkeeping divergence or a measurement-access change

nodes.definition: Treat the chemistry supplier's laboratory as the deep end of the analysis toolkit: a properly drawn sample (level restored, bath mixed, clean labeled container, bath identity and recent history attached) buys a full profile — metal contents, trim species, contaminant metals, additive status — that no bench method reaches, plus the supplier's product-specific interpretation against their own TDS. It is the arbiter when bench titrations disagree with the deposit's story, the escalation partner when drift defies bench diagnosis, and the periodic deep check that catches slow composition creep the weekly methods never resolve. Its costs shape its role: days of turnaround and a fee per sample mean it anchors the cadence rather than running it, and a shop that ships a sloppy sample buys a confident analysis of the wrong liquid. Lab results govern composition disputes; the bench recalibrates its own methods against them.

included: correct sampling procedure and history attachment
full-profile and contaminant-level analysis as a service class
excluded: acting on contamination findings (lifecycle KB)
same-day control decisions (bench methods)

pros.claim: The lab sees the species the bench cannot, closing the diagnostic gap honestly instead of by guesswork
pros.example: persistent slight dullness with all bench numbers in window comes back from the lab as a trace metallic contaminant profile — and routes correctly to lifecycle treatment instead of another additive dose

cons.claim: Turnaround and cost make the lab useless for same-day decisions and tempt shops to skip it entirely
cons.example: a rush week passes on the quarterly deep check to save the fee, and the slow hardener creep it would have caught surfaces later as a color complaint

failure_modes: sampling a low, unmixed bath and shipping an artifact
sending no bath history so the lab interprets blind
ignoring the lab schedule until a crisis forces it
acceptance_tests: each lab submission logs the sampling procedure, attached history and result against the TDS window; bench methods are recalibrated after any bench-vs-lab divergence
revisit_triggers: a bench-vs-lab divergence
the supplier changes lab offerings or the shop changes supplier

base.update_signal: a lab result overturning a bench inference or a supplier service change

nodes.definition: Assemble the method classes into a schedule matched to the shop's throughput: the deposit is read every run; the cheap bench checks (pH, temperature verification, level) ride a short cycle; titrations follow the TDS scheme's frequency scaled by actual work through the tank; coupons anchor the rate on a longer cycle; and the supplier lab takes the periodic deep check. Onto the calendar go the event triggers that pull any check forward regardless of schedule — a drift signature appears, a correction was made, an idle period ends, a defect emerges, a new lot of replenisher starts. The cadence also carries this KB's counterintuitive centerpiece for jeweler-scale shops: a low-throughput bath is not a low-maintenance bath, because evaporation, air absorption and additive aging continue while nothing plates, so idle time earns its own checks rather than exempting the bath from them.

included: per-method cadence assignment scaled to throughput
event triggers that force out-of-schedule checks
idle-time checks as first-class cadence entries
excluded: the methods' own mechanics (their nodes)
production QC sampling of finished goods (quality specialist)

pros.claim: A written cadence converts bath control from mood-driven to evidence-driven and survives operator changes
pros.example: the relief operator covering a holiday week runs the same checks off the card and calendar instead of what they personally remember to worry about

cons.claim: A cadence calibrated to last year's throughput silently under-checks a bath whose duty doubled
cons.example: a new trade account triples work through the hard gold while titrations stay monthly, and drift now outruns the schedule between checks

failure_modes: cadence copied from another shop's throughput
event triggers absent, so upsets wait for the next scheduled check
idle baths dropped from the calendar entirely
acceptance_tests: every method class has a cadence entry tied to current throughput, the event-trigger list is written on the card, and idle baths appear on the calendar with their own checks
revisit_triggers: throughput changes materially in either direction
an upset occurs that no trigger caught
trend review shows drift outrunning the schedule

base.update_signal: a throughput change or an upset that slipped between scheduled checks

nodes.definition: Dose the bath the way it is depleted — continuously and in small amounts: additions sized from ampere-minute bookkeeping cross-checked by the latest analysis, using the TDS replenisher scheme (gold salt or replenisher concentrate, trim chemicals, additives) in the increments the supplier designed the product around, each addition made to a level-restored bath, stirred in, and logged at the tank when made. The mechanism case is stability: small in-window doses keep every parameter near the middle of its band, whereas letting the bath drift and dosing big swings it across the window, and a swing invites the counter-dose that starts oscillation — each cycle of which shows up on customer pieces as color and brightness wander. The discipline's enemies are convenience batching ('I'll do it all Friday'), unlogged favors by a second pair of hands, and the round-number dose that ignores what the log says was actually consumed.

included: dose sizing from bookkeeping plus analysis
oscillation avoidance as the governing mechanism
excluded: large-excursion recovery (crash-correction node)
byproduct and contamination removal (lifecycle KB)

pros.claim: Little-and-often keeps deposits consistent enough that color matching across a multi-week order holds
pros.example: a forty-piece trade order plated over three weeks stays within the customer's color tolerance because gold and trim never left mid-window

cons.claim: Frequent small doses multiply the chances for an unlogged or mis-sized addition on a busy bench
cons.example: two small gold additions in one afternoon, one logged and one not, and the week's bookkeeping is quietly wrong by one dose

failure_modes: batching additions for convenience until the bath has already drifted
dosing round numbers instead of consumption-based amounts
additions by a second operator bypassing the log
acceptance_tests: every addition in the log shows its sizing basis (ampere-minutes and/or analysis), its TDS scheme line, and same-time recording; bath parameters trend mid-window rather than sawtoothing
revisit_triggers: parameters sawtooth in the trend
a reconciliation finds unlogged additions
the supplier revises the replenisher scheme

base.update_signal: sawtooth trends, unlogged additions surfacing, or a replenisher-scheme revision

nodes.definition: When little-and-often has lapsed and the bath sits far from its window, recover it by protocol, not heroics: establish the full picture first (analysis of every reachable parameter, level restored, temperature verified), then correct one variable at a time in TDS-sized increments with analysis between steps, proving each stage on a Hull cell panel or coupon before the next, and never exceeding the addition increments the TDS sanctions in pursuit of speed — a one-shot restoration invites overshoot, and overshoot invites the counter-dose spiral that ends worse than the original drift. The safety envelope binds harder here than anywhere: a stressed operator reaching for a fast correction is exactly when a forbidden chemical shortcut looks tempting. And the protocol carries its own exit: if two staged passes fail to bring the bath in, or the correction arithmetic implies additions outside the TDS scheme, the bath's problem is not replenishment — it routes to the supplier and to lifecycle disposition with the log attached.

included: one-variable-at-a-time staging with proof between steps
TDS increment ceilings under time pressure
the two-failures exit to supplier and lifecycle
excluded: regenerate-vs-replace economics and remake execution (lifecycle KB)
any correction chemical the TDS does not name

pros.claim: Staging with proof between steps converts an unbounded gamble into a sequence of small reversible bets
pros.example: a neglected hard gold gets its gold restored first, panel-checked, then pH trimmed, panel-checked again — and the second panel reveals the hue issue was pH all along, sparing a hardener addition that would have overshot

cons.claim: Staged recovery takes bench days the schedule may not want to give
cons.example: a wedding order waits while the bath comes back over two days of stage-analyze-verify — the cost of the neglect that preceded it, but paid now

failure_modes: one big multi-chemical addition to save time
correcting two variables in one step so neither effect is attributable
skipping the proof panel between stages
pressing past two failed passes instead of escalating
acceptance_tests: every crash correction in the log shows the pre-correction full analysis, single-variable staged additions each within TDS increments, proof artifacts between stages, and either in-window closure or a documented escalation
revisit_triggers: a correction requires more than the TDS-sanctioned increments
the same bath needs crash correction twice in a season

base.update_signal: a failed staged recovery or a correction that pressed against TDS increment ceilings

nodes.definition: Keep one log per bath as the shop's institutional memory and legal-grade evidence line: every run's date, ampere-minutes, temperature and pH readings, every addition with its size and sizing basis, every analysis result with its method, every coupon and panel with where it is filed, every deposit observation, every excursion and what was done about it. The log is what turns 'the bath has been getting warmer-toned lately' from a feeling into a queryable trend; it is the first thing the supplier's technical service asks for when a bath misbehaves; it is how a second operator or a future hire inherits the bath instead of restarting the learning curve; and it is where the shop's own refined operating points — always inside the TDS window — earn their standing, because they are demonstrated in ink rather than remembered. The integrity rule is absolute: an event that is not logged did not, for control purposes, happen — and a bath with a known-incomplete log is treated as unknown until re-verified.

included: the log as supplier-service and handover artifact
in-window shop refinements evidenced in the log
excluded: job/thickness records tied to customer claims (quality and process specialists)
waste manifests (safety specialist)

pros.claim: The log makes slow drift visible that no individual run can show
pros.example: six weeks of entries reveal pH trim consumption doubling while throughput held flat — a trend invisible day to day that flags a developing problem worth the supplier's eyes

cons.claim: Logging is friction on every run, and friction gets skipped exactly on the busiest days when the most happens to the bath
cons.example: during the pre-holiday rush the additions all happen but half the entries do not, gutting the very weeks the trend review most needs

failure_modes: entries reconstructed from memory at week's end
two logs or loose notes for one bath
additions by helpers bypassing the log entirely
acceptance_tests: each bath has exactly one log; spot-checking any recent week finds every run, addition, analysis and observation present with dates; the mandatory-field list is written inside the log's cover
revisit_triggers: a spot-check finds gaps
a second operator joins the bench
the supplier requests history the log cannot answer

base.update_signal: a log gap discovered, or a question the log should answer but cannot

nodes.definition: Read the log on a fixed rhythm and decide: for each bath, plot or eyeball the lines — parameter readings against their TDS bands, addition frequency and size, byproduct growth, coupon rates, deposit observations — and classify what they show. A special-cause spike (one bad day, traceable to an event) gets a targeted response; slow secular creep across weeks gets a scheduled correction and possibly a cadence tightening; a bath whose corrections grow larger and more frequent while results worsen is aging, and aging is not a maintenance problem — it is the evidence package that opens the lifecycle KB's regenerate-vs-replace question, handed over with the log rather than argued from impressions. The review is also where the maintenance system audits itself: triggers that never fire, checks that never move a decision, and cadences that always arrive after the drift are all findings, and each one feeds an adjustment. The output is a dated decision — watch, correct, or escalate — with the evidence line it rests on named.

included: the aging evidence package for lifecycle handoff
excluded: executing the lifecycle decision (lifecycle KB)
single-run responses (drift signature node)

pros.claim: The review catches the drift class that per-run vigilance is structurally blind to
pros.example: every individual Friday check looked fine, but the monthly review shows gold additions growing steadily for constant throughput — falling efficiency, invisible except in aggregate

cons.claim: Trend reading over-fits noise when the data is sparse, which jeweler-scale logs often are
cons.example: three points drifting 'up' over six weeks on a lightly used bath is as likely sampling scatter as signal — the review must resist correcting on it

failure_modes: reviews skipped until a crisis forces a retrospective
every wiggle treated as signal, driving needless corrections
aging evidence accumulating without the lifecycle question ever being raised
acceptance_tests: reviews happen on the stated rhythm and each produces a dated watch/correct/escalate decision naming its evidence line; aging handoffs include the log extract
revisit_triggers: a decision proves wrong in hindsight
the review rhythm lags the bath's actual rate of change

base.update_signal: a hindsight-wrong decision or a drift that outran the review rhythm

nodes.definition: Enforce the line that gives every other node its teeth: the moment any parameter reads outside its TDS window — or the bath's state is simply unknown because the log has a hole — customer work on that bath stops. No 'one more piece', no finishing the tray: an out-of-window bath produces deposits whose color, thickness, adhesion or safety standing cannot be vouched for, and a plated customer heirloom is not strippable for free. The path back is defined, not discretionary: correct per the appropriate protocol, re-analyze to show every parameter in window, then plate and pass a test piece — coupon or panel meeting the retained standard — before the first customer piece re-enters. Excursion, response and requalification are written back to the log as one linked entry, because the excursion record is both the shop's learning material and its honest answer if a batch plated near the event is ever questioned. Where a floor is involved the stop is a safety response and overrides everything, including this node's own re-entry sequence, in favor of the safety envelope's rules.

included: the stop rule on any out-of-window or unknown state
the defined re-entry sequence (correct, re-analyze, test piece)
excluded: the correction mechanics (crash-correction node)
customer communication about delays (business specialist)

pros.claim: A bright-line stop rule removes the per-job negotiation in which deadline pressure always wins
pros.example: with the rule posted on the tank, the question 'can we just run these six pendants first' has a standing answer that nobody has to argue afresh at 5 pm

cons.claim: A stop rule invites quiet circumvention if the shop's economics never budgeted for stoppage
cons.example: a bench that promised same-day turnaround on everything discovers operators 'not noticing' borderline readings — the rule needs slack in the promise-making upstream

failure_modes: plating through a known excursion to meet a date
resuming after correction without the test piece
excursions handled but never written up, so the same one recurs
acceptance_tests: the stop rule is posted per bath; every excursion in the log links its response and requalification test piece; no customer-work entry falls inside a stop period
revisit_triggers: an excursion is discovered to have been plated through
requalification criteria prove too loose or too strict in hindsight

base.update_signal: a plated-through excursion surfacing or a requalification criterion failing in hindsight

nodes.definition: Own the jeweler-scale reality that baths spend most of their life not plating: an idle heated bath keeps evaporating, an idle alkaline bath keeps absorbing carbon dioxide and growing carbonate, additives keep aging, and a cold unstirred tank stratifies — so weeks of idleness change the bath as surely as work does, only invisibly. Idle care is cheap and specific: keep the tank covered and labeled, hold or restore level on a light cadence, and keep the idle bath on the calendar rather than out of sight. Restart is a gate, not a resumption: before the first customer piece after a meaningful idle period, restore level and temperature, stir to homogenize, verify pH, run the analysis the idle length warrants, and plate a test coupon against the retained standard. The classic small-shop failure this node exists to kill is the confident first job straight into a bath nobody has touched since last month — with a customer's piece as the unwitting test coupon.

included: idle-time drift mechanisms (evaporation, air absorption, additive aging, stratification)
the restart verification gate with test coupon
excluded: long-term storage or decommissioning of a bath (lifecycle KB)
restart of a bath after contamination treatment (lifecycle KB)

pros.claim: A restart gate converts the riskiest run of the month — the first one — into the best-verified
pros.example: after a four-week lull the restart coupon comes out hazy, the pH check finds drift, and the correction happens before the customer's locket rather than on it

cons.claim: Restart verification adds lead time to exactly the impulse jobs a quiet shop most wants to say yes to
cons.example: a walk-in wants one ring replated today; the honest answer after a long idle spell is tomorrow, and some walk-ins walk out

failure_modes: first job after idleness plated with no verification
idle baths uncovered and off the calendar
restart checks skipped because the last run, weeks ago, was fine
acceptance_tests: idle baths appear on the care calendar; every restart after the shop's defined idle threshold shows level, temperature, pH, warranted analysis and a passing test coupon logged before customer work
revisit_triggers: a restart coupon fails
the shop's idle patterns change (seasonality, new account)

base.update_signal: a failed restart coupon or a change in the shop's idle rhythm

edges.why_related: the mechanism map interprets readings against the windows the control card extracted from the TDS
the gold band being tracked and the replenisher scheme sizing additions both come from the TDS card
pH watching presumes knowing what pH does to efficiency, deposit character and hue, and which way each bath naturally drifts
temperature and agitation control rest on their mechanism roles: efficiency, color, hardness and the limiting current density
additive management presumes the mechanism by which hardener metal and brighteners set hardness, brightness and hue
byproduct watching presumes the mechanism that carbonate and additive-breakdown accumulation dull the deposit and drag efficiency
a signature only narrows the suspect list if the reader holds the parameter-to-symptom mechanism map
pH floors are stop conditions and trim chemistry is bounded by the cyanide/acid segregation line
titrating a cyanide bath is cyanide handling: trained persons, PPE, and segregated reagents and drains
agitation method choice excludes air sparging of cyanide baths because aerosolized mist is an exposure route
corrections under stress are where forbidden chemical shortcuts look tempting; the envelope bounds what is even considerable
the commercial-products-only line means additives are dosed strictly per the TDS scheme, never improvised or substituted
when correction arithmetic exceeds the TDS scheme the problem stops being maintenance and routes to supplier and lifecycle
dose sizing starts from the ampere-minute consumption estimate the gold bookkeeping maintains
the cadence schedules titration as its in-house backbone, at frequencies the TDS scheme and throughput set
the cadence assigns the panel its diagnostic and before/after-correction roles rather than a fixed calendar slot
little-and-often dosing leans on the cadence delivering fresh-enough analyses to cross-check the bookkeeping
a staged recovery starts from the signature-led hypothesis of which parameter classes moved
crash correction is the successor state entered only when the little-and-often discipline has lapsed or failed
analyze before dosing: the addition follows the reading that justifies it, never the other way around
the review can only read trends the log actually recorded; a gapped log caps what review can conclude
per-run deposit observations are one of the trend lines the periodic review classifies
the review's correct-or-escalate decisions invoke the stop-and-requalify rule when a window is breached
the re-entry sequence after an excursion runs the staged-correction protocol as its correction step
restart verification begins with level restoration because idleness concentrates the bath by evaporation
the cadence's idle-time entries and event triggers define which checks a restart of given idle length warrants
falling gold content lowers the limiting current density, which surfaces as the burning-threshold-creep signature the reader watches for
accumulating byproducts dull and haze the deposit, producing the signature class the reader must distinguish from contamination
evaporation concentrates the solution, so an unrestored level distorts the apparent gold content every bookkeeping reconciliation relies on
measured coupon rates correct the efficiency assumption inside the ampere-minute dose sizing
review findings — drift outrunning checks, triggers that never fire — retune the cadence and its event triggers
every excursion, response and requalification is written back as a linked log entry, enriching the evidence base the next review reads
the bench panel suggests a same-day interpretation while the definitive composition answer is days away at the lab, and acting on the panel can pre-empt the lab's contrary finding
edges.resolution_rule: bench methods gate same-day in-window trims only; any correction that changes composition materially waits for or is bounded by lab confirmation, and when lab and bench disagree the lab governs composition while the bench recalibrates

edges.why_related: dosing an additive to chase an appearance symptom can mask the underlying cause the signature was pointing at, destroying the diagnostic trail
edges.resolution_rule: no additive is dosed without an analysis-backed or TDS-scheduled reason; if the symptom persists after one in-window trim, further dosing stops and the case escalates to diagnosis instead of repetition

edges.why_related: a deep excursion tempts additions beyond the increments the TDS sanctions, pitting recovery speed against the setpoint authority
edges.resolution_rule: the TDS wins: corrections stage within TDS-sanctioned increments, and if in-window recovery is arithmetically impossible inside the scheme, the bath escalates to the supplier and to lifecycle disposition rather than being forced

edges.why_related: both are quantitative verification classes — one measures the solution's composition, the other measures the deposit the solution actually produced — and each covers the other's blind side

conflict_axes.name: tds_authority_vs_shop_lore
conflict_axes.description: The supplier's TDS window versus the bench's accumulated habits ('it runs better a bit warm') that drift the bath off its documented footing.
poles: operate strictly to the TDS window
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the TDS governs; shop refinements are legitimate only inside the window and only when demonstrated in the log, not remembered

conflict_axes.name: little_and_often_vs_batch_convenience
conflict_axes.description: Dosing small amounts on the consumption rhythm versus saving all additions for one convenient weekly session while the bath drifts between.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the dosing rhythm follows depletion, not the calendar's convenience; batching is acceptable only when bookkeeping shows depletion still leaves every parameter mid-window

conflict_axes.name: deadline_throughput_vs_stop_rule
conflict_axes.description: A promised delivery date versus a bath reading out of window — the recurring collision where quality and safety discipline is actually tested.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the stop rule wins every time; safety floors are absolute and quality windows admit no 'one more piece' — the schedule fix belongs upstream in promise-making

conflict_axes.name: bench_speed_vs_lab_accuracy
conflict_axes.description: Same-day bench readings (titration, panel) versus the supplier lab's slower but deeper and product-authoritative analysis.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: bench methods run the day-to-day loop; composition-changing corrections and bench-vs-deposit contradictions wait for the lab, which governs composition disputes

conflict_axes.name: analysis_cost_vs_drift_risk
conflict_axes.description: Analysis time, coupon gold and lab fees on a thin-margin bench versus the compounding cost of plating on an unverified bath.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: scale cadence to throughput rather than skipping classes of check; the cheapest checks (deposit read, pH, level) are never the ones to cut, and customer work on an unknown bath is the one expense never taken

conflict_axes.name: additive_dose_vs_root_cause
conflict_axes.description: Chasing appearance with another additive shot versus holding off to diagnose which parameter actually moved.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: analysis precedes addition; one in-window trim is the maximum response to an undiagnosed symptom, and recurrence escalates to diagnosis

conflict_axes.name: correction_speed_vs_overshoot
conflict_axes.description: Restoring a drifted bath in one decisive addition versus staging small increments with verification between, at the cost of bench days.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: stage within TDS increments with analysis and a panel or coupon between steps; the time saved by one-shot dosing is repaid with interest by the overshoot-counter-dose spiral

conflict_axes.name: safety_floor_vs_process_convenience
conflict_axes.description: Conveniences that would help the process — air agitation for mass transfer, a fast acid trim, shared drains — versus the cyanide/acid segregation line and published-chemistry floors.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: safety wins unconditionally: no acid near cyanide chemistry ever, no aerosolizing agitation of cyanide baths, floors are stop conditions — no throughput or cost argument reopens these

conflict_axes.name: log_discipline_vs_bench_time
conflict_axes.description: Complete per-run logging versus the minutes it costs on the busiest days — which are precisely the days the most happens to the bath.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: hold a small mandatory field set that fits on one line and is filled at the tank when the event happens; an unlogged bath is treated as unknown, which costs far more time than the entry would have

conflict_axes.name: maintain_vs_lifecycle_handoff
conflict_axes.description: Keeping an aging bath alive with ever-larger corrections versus raising the regenerate-or-replace question that belongs to lifecycle economics.
poles: hand the aging question to lifecycle
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: when corrections grow in size and frequency while results worsen, or a staged recovery fails twice, maintenance stops arguing and hands over the log as an evidence package — the decision itself is out of this KB's scope

edge_cases.description: Edges scorch at the exact current settings that plated clean last week
edge_cases.trigger: the burning threshold creeps down because gold content fell or agitation weakened while settings stayed constant
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as a bath signal, not a settings problem: analyze gold against the TDS band, check agitation, replenish per the scheme, and verify recovery on a coupon before customer work

edge_cases.description: The pH meter reads comfortably in-window but has not seen a calibration buffer in months
edge_cases.trigger: stale calibration produces a confident wrong reading that hides real drift or invents phantom drift
edge_cases.mitigation: calibration on a logged schedule is a precondition for trusting any reading; an uncalibrated meter's readings are treated as unknown bath state, which stops customer work until re-measured

edge_cases.description: An acid hard gold's pH has crept down near its TDS floor mid-week
edge_cases.trigger: normal anodic acid generation accumulates faster than the trim cadence assumed
edge_cases.mitigation: stop plating at the floor approach — published chemistry makes low pH in cyanide-complex baths an HCN hazard, not a quality nuance; trim upward only with the TDS-named chemical and requalify before resuming

edge_cases.description: Color has drifted slightly warmer over three weeks though every single-run check looked fine
edge_cases.trigger: slow hardener or pH creep too small for any one run to flag accumulates across many runs
edge_cases.mitigation: the periodic trend review compares deposit observations across weeks against the retained standard and dispatches hardener and pH analysis when the aggregate line moves, before any customer rejects it

edge_cases.description: After a long bookkeeping lapse, one big compensating gold addition overshoots the window
edge_cases.trigger: a crash correction sized in one shot from an uncertain baseline
edge_cases.mitigation: re-baseline with a fresh analysis first, then stage additions in TDS increments with analysis between; never dose to a guess of what was missed

edge_cases.description: First customer job goes straight into a bath idle for six weeks
edge_cases.trigger: idle-time drift (evaporation, air absorption, additive aging, stratification) is invisible so restart feels safe
edge_cases.mitigation: the restart gate: restore level and temperature, homogenize, verify pH, run the warranted analysis, and pass a test coupon before any customer piece

edge_cases.description: The Hull cell panel is clean but production pieces come out dull
edge_cases.trigger: either the panel was run at non-production conditions, or the fault is prep/process rather than chemistry
edge_cases.mitigation: re-run the panel mimicking production temperature and agitation; if still clean, the bath is exonerated and the fault routes to prep or process investigation instead of chemical additions

edge_cases.description: Temperature and gold content drifted low together and their symptoms confound
edge_cases.trigger: two parameters moved at once, so correcting the visible one masks the other
edge_cases.mitigation: verify the cheap physical variables (temperature, level, agitation) before chemical analysis, then correct one variable at a time with a check between — never both in one step

edge_cases.description: Brightener dosed on a hunch against haze; the haze returns worse
edge_cases.trigger: the symptom's cause was accumulating byproducts or organic load, which more additive cannot fix and may worsen
edge_cases.mitigation: no additive without an analysis-backed reason; recurring haze checks the byproduct trend first and then routes to contamination/lifecycle diagnosis with the log, not to a third dose

edge_cases.description: A helper runs the weekly free-cyanide titration without cyanide training
edge_cases.trigger: analysis work is mentally filed as 'lab work' and escapes the tank-side safety envelope
edge_cases.mitigation: titrating cyanide is cyanide handling: named trained persons only, same PPE and segregation classes as the tank, or the determination is outsourced to the supplier lab

edge_cases.description: The supplier lab's gold result contradicts the bench titration run the same day
edge_cases.trigger: sampling error, stale reagents or endpoint misreading on the bench — or a mislabeled lab sample
edge_cases.mitigation: re-check the sampling procedure on both sides; absent a sampling fault the lab governs composition, the bench method is recalibrated against it, and no correction is made on the disputed number meanwhile

edge_cases.description: The log looks complete but a second operator made additions that were never entered
edge_cases.trigger: informal help during a rush bypasses the log, silently corrupting the trend and the bookkeeping
edge_cases.mitigation: one log per bath, entries at the tank at the time, by whoever acts; once unlogged additions surface, the bath's state is unknown — full analysis before further customer work, and the gap is written up

workflow.action: Extract each bath's TDS into a bench control card
workflow.description: Pull windows, trim and replenisher chemicals, analysis scheme and product/lot identity out of the supplier TDS onto a card at the tank
workflow.artifact: per-bath control card with TDS revision date
workflow.gate: every controlled parameter shows a TDS-sourced window and named trim chemical; product, lot and TDS revision are recorded

workflow.action: Confirm the safety envelope for all maintenance work
workflow.description: Verify segregation of cyanide and acid chemistry, storage and drain separation, PPE and ventilation classes, training records and the jurisdiction check
workflow.artifact: maintenance safety checklist with training roster
workflow.gate: no maintenance step brings acid near cyanide chemistry; floors are posted as stop conditions; only trained, named persons analyze or dose

workflow.action: Write the parameter-effect and drift-signature sheet for each bath type
workflow.description: Document what each parameter does to the deposit and the symptom of drift in each direction, as mechanisms without invented numbers
workflow.gate: each parameter has a direction-of-effect and drift symptom stated; no numeric setpoint appears that is not a TDS citation

workflow.action: Open the bath log with its mandatory field set
workflow.description: One log per bath: run data, additions, analyses, observations, excursions, with the field list inside the cover
workflow.gate: the log exists, is the only record for its bath, and its mandatory fields cover ampere-minutes, temperature, pH, additions, analyses and deposit observations

workflow.action: Stand up the analysis method classes and assign responsibilities
workflow.description: Establish in-house titration and panel capability, coupon and XRF access, and the supplier-lab sampling procedure, each with named trained owners
workflow.artifact: method-class register with owners and limits
workflow.gate: every control question maps to a method class with its limits noted and a trained owner named

workflow.action: Schedule the analysis cadence with event triggers
workflow.description: Assign each method class a frequency scaled to throughput, add idle-bath entries, and write the event triggers that pull checks forward
